A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LRAM study. Their text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–G support reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: V2 reports original multi-domain evaluations, fine-tuning, Dark-Room in-context learning, inference measurements and ablations in Section 4 and Appendices D–G.

after.justification: V3 retains those empirical results and adds Mamba inference measurements, an xLSTM head-count ablation and Mamba embedding analysis.

M1.justification: The proposed LRAM procedure retains its backbones, action-free input sequence, shared discretized action head, cross-entropy objective and recurrent inference. Additional head configurations are evaluated as experimental variants.

E1.justification: Both use the same 432 training tasks across six domains, 37 held-out tasks, Dark-Room 10×10 and Atari Freeway timing environment. The added measurements do not introduce different task or dataset coverage.

E2.justification: Mamba joins the DT–xLSTM latency, memory and throughput comparisons in Figures 6–7 and the embedding comparison in Figure 34. The comparator sets for the original benchmark evaluations remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The added timing experiments include layer/parameter-matched Mamba without torch.compile and xLSTM configurations with 4, 8, 16 and 32 heads at fixed hidden width. Existing training budgets, splits and evaluation metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix D.5.4 and Figure 22 test throughput sensitivity to head dimension. Appendix F extends the existing embedding analysis to Mamba. Earlier context-length, action-removal, return-conditioning, layer-ratio, dropout and layer-count ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Both retain mean and 95% confidence-interval reporting over three seeds, evaluation-seed averaging and the stated single-run exceptions for selected experiments. No changed uncertainty-estimation practice or run count is documented.

E6.justification: V3 adds Mamba timings, head-count throughput results and Mamba embedding findings. Existing timing values also change: Figure 6 reports DT latency around 7.8 ms versus 5.4 ms at B=16, C=3200, although Figure 17 retains the earlier value. Benchmark score Tables 8–16 and original learning curves are unchanged.

T1.justification: The RL and Decision Transformer definitions and Equations 1–2 are retained. Added complexity and head-dimension explanations introduce no new formal derivation, assumption, theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list retain the same proposal and performance/efficiency claims. Mamba's long-context advantages are more explicit in v3's conclusion, but were already asserted in v2's Introduction.

C2.justification: V3 explains Mamba's latency disadvantage through compilation incompatibility, discusses head dimension's computational cost, and qualifies embedding separation as potentially dependent on the task mixture. Appendices B.1 and C.1 add dataset-selection and equal-domain-weighting rationales. Existing deployment limitations remain.

D1.justification: V3 documents Mamba's kernel source and compilation incompatibility, alongside settings for the new head-count experiments. Appendix A removes the statement that source code accompanies the supplementary material while retaining the same public code/data link.

R1.justification: The bibliography contains the same works, and the related-work positioning remains substantively unchanged. Citations used in the expanded explanations were already present in v2.

P1.justification: V3 makes widespread small grammar and terminology corrections, expands targeted explanations, updates acknowledgements and adds publication text. The main narrative and section organization remain largely intact.

P2.justification: Figures 6–7 gain series and revised legends/axes. New Figure 22 displays the head-count ablation; Figure 34 adds Mamba while redisplaying the original DT/xLSTM embedding panels. Existing appendix figures are renumbered and floats relocated.

improvement.justification: Adding Mamba inference comparisons and the head-dimension ablation makes the efficiency argument more complete, while implementation caveats and qualified embedding interpretations improve its assessment. Updated Figure 6 latencies conflict with retained Figure 17 values, introducing a localized consistency problem. The added comparative and diagnostic evidence nevertheless supports a limited net improvement.
